# tScrub — Verifiable Disk Sanitisation

tScrub is an open, auditable data-erasure tool for regulated IT. It erases NVMe, SATA, and SCSI drives to NIST 800-88 Clear, Purge, and Destroy levels, then hands you a chain-of-custody report your auditors can actually read. It is a single self-contained Bash script — your security team can inspect every line of what runs on the appliance. You build your own appliance: boot from USB or PXE on hardware you already own. No locked-down vendor box required.

## What it does

- **NVMe sanitise** — crypto, block, and overwrite sanitise, plus format fallback, with live SSTAT progress monitoring.
- **ATA secure erase** — enhanced and standard security erase for SATA/ATA drives, with frozen-drive handling.
- **SCSI sanitise** — for SAS/SCSI drives.
- **SED / OPAL unlock** — PSID revert for locked self-encrypting drives, plus detection of BIOS Block SID lockdown (0x4286).
- **Chain of custody** — COCID, system serials, and per-drive final status in a single CSV report for the whole job.
- **SMART capture** — pre/post-wipe SMART health (status, temperature, power-on hours, wear) recorded per drive.
- **Verifiable proof of destruction** — reports can be signed (SHA-256 + Ed25519), producing a sidecar signature and manifest that auditors can independently verify.

## How it works (four steps)

1. **Boot** — boot Linux from USB or PXE and run the script; tScrub needs zero installation.
2. **Discover & classify** — every drive is detected and mapped to its best Purge or Clear capability.
3. **Sanitise** — live progress across all drives, with frozen and blocked drives flagged.
4. **Report** — a chain-of-custody CSV with method, certification, final status, and pre/post-wipe SMART per drive.

## Compliance

- Maps each wipe method to NIST 800-88 Clear, Purge, and Destroy outcomes.
- Chain-of-custody reporting supports GDPR, HIPAA, and ISO 27001 programmes.
- Financial services (FCA/PRA), healthcare (UK GDPR/NHS), ITAD & refurbishers, and data centres are primary audiences.

## Comparison vs Blancco

tScrub is the open, auditable alternative to Blancco for verifiable disk sanitisation — same compliance outcome, no vendor lock-in. It is inspectable (single script), appliance-agnostic (your own hardware), and produces verifiable, signed reports.

## Pricing & download

- **Free** — community build: full erasure with unsigned (checksum-only) reports; a free licence is required.
- **Pay-as-you-go** — £0.25 per device for signed reports.
- **Team** — £99/month for signed reports and support.
- **Enterprise** — custom pricing for regulated fleets.

Choose a plan and request the download on the Download page (https://tscrub.com/download).

## Getting started

Issue your licence on the Download page (account required) and download the tScrub script from your dashboard's Licence page. Boot a Linux live environment (ShredOS or your own) from USB or PXE, place the `.lic` alongside `tscrub.sh`, and run it. At the end of a run the appliance writes the report locally (boot USB, or `tscrub_output=`) and can push it to your dashboard (`tscrub_upload=` + `tscrub_api_token=`) or FTP (`shredos_output=`). Verify reports with the `tscrub verify` command (documented in the Docs page).

## Certificate of Destruction

Upload a tScrub report (CSV + JSON manifest + optional signature) at tscrub.com/dashboard/certify (account required) to verify it and generate a printable PDF Certificate of Destruction per Chain of Custody ID. Certificates include a device annex (Annex A) and — when present in the report — a pre/post-wipe SMART capture annex (Annex B: status, temperature, power-on hours, wear). Generated certificates are listed on the same page for download and management.

## SMART data reports

Per-drive details and pre/post-wipe SMART data for every certificate are available at tscrub.com/dashboard/reports: device, type, model, serial, sanitisation method, certification, final status, and before/after SMART attributes (status, temperature, power-on hours, power cycles, wear, TBW).
